issues.title: Logic inversion in hasPendingInviteByUserId method
issues.description: The hasPendingInviteByUserId method checks for accepted:true memberships instead of accepted:false (pending invites). This inverts the method's logic - it will return true when users have accepted team memberships rather than pending invites. This breaks the onboarding flow for users with team invites, causing users with accepted memberships to be redirected to personal onboarding instead of users with pending invites. The method name and its intended purpose clearly indicate it should check for pending (non-accepted) invites.

issues.title: Incorrect conditional operator in onboarding redirect logic
issues.description: The conditional logic for redirecting users with pending invites uses OR (||) instead of AND (&&). This means users will be redirected to '/onboarding/personal/settings' if they have a pending invite OR if onboarding-v3 is enabled, rather than requiring both conditions. This breaks the normal onboarding flow - any user with onboarding-v3 enabled will be incorrectly redirected to personal settings regardless of whether they have pending invites. The intended behavior was to only redirect users who have both onboarding-v3 enabled AND a pending invite.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26829 - fix: add server-side redirect for users with pending invites on onboarding page

structured_output.summary:
The PR adds a server-side check to `/onboarding/getting-started` so invited users skip plan selection and go straight to `/onboarding/personal/settings`. It also moves the inline `prisma.membership.findFirst` from `onboardingUtils.ts` into a new static method, `MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId`, and adds integration tests for that method.

The idea is right, but two logic errors break it. First, the new repository method filters on `accepted: true`. It reports a pending invite for anyone who has already joined a team, and never for someone who is actually invited. Second, `checkOnboardingRedirect` changed `pendingInvite && onboardingV3Enabled` to `hasPendingInvite || onboardingV3Enabled`. That sends every v3 user to personal settings (so the plan-selection page can never be reached from this path) and sends invited users on legacy onboarding to a v3-only route. Combined, the fix doesn't work for invited users, and existing team members visiting getting-started get redirected away. The new tests would catch the first bug, but one of them uses a conditional assertion that can pass without testing anything.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The new repository method checks the opposite condition (`accepted: true`), and the redirect condition in `onboardingUtils.ts` was changed from `&&` to `||`. Together they break the core onboarding redirect logic for both invited and non-invited users.

architecture.overview:
Onboarding routing is decided in two places on the server. `checkOnboardingRedirect` in `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts` is called from `apps/web/app/page.tsx` and from the event-types page. For users who haven't finished onboarding, it picks the legacy `/getting-started` flow or the v3 `/onboarding/*` flow based on the `onboarding-v3` feature flag. Before this PR, the only special case was users with a pending membership (`accepted: false`) when v3 was enabled: they went straight to `/onboarding/personal/settings`.

The PR moves the pending-invite lookup into a new static method, `MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId`. It also adds a second guard inside the `/onboarding/getting-started` server page, so invited users who land there directly (for example after signing up with an invite token) are redirected before the plan-selection view renders.
steps: Entry points: `apps/web/app/page.tsx` and `(main-nav)/event-types/page.tsx` call `checkOnboardingRedirect(userId)` for users who haven't completed onboarding.
`checkOnboardingRedirect` checks email verification, reads the `onboarding-v3` flag, and now calls `MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId` instead of querying prisma inline.
Its branch condition decides between `/onboarding/personal/settings`, `/onboarding/getting-started` and the legacy `/getting-started`.
New: the `/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx` server component calls the same repository method after the session check and redirects to `/onboarding/personal/settings` when it returns true.
`MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId` runs a `findFirst` on the `Membership` table filtered by `userId` plus an `accepted` predicate, and returns a boolean.
`MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts` runs the method against a real DB, creating users and memberships.

findings.title: `hasPendingInviteByUserId` queries `accepted: true`, so it detects accepted memberships instead of pending ones
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.ts`, the new static method `hasPendingInviteByUserId` (around lines 584-595) filters memberships with `accepted: true`, which is the opposite of a pending invite. Change the filter to `accepted: false`, matching the original inline query that was removed from `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts`. Then run `MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts` and confirm the pending and accepted cases pass.

findings.title: Redirect condition changed from `&&` to `||`, so every v3 user skips plan selection
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts` around line 69, the condition was changed from `pendingInvite && onboardingV3Enabled` to `hasPendingInvite || onboardingV3Enabled`. That sends every v3 user to `/onboarding/personal/settings`, makes the `/onboarding/getting-started` return unreachable, and sends legacy (non-v3) invited users to a v3 route. Restore `&&` so the refactor keeps the original behaviour. Consider adding a unit test for `checkOnboardingRedirect` that covers all four combinations of the pending-invite and v3 flags.

findings.title: Mixed-invite test can pass without testing anything
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts`, the test 'should return true when user has both accepted and pending invites' (lines ~117-162) looks up an arbitrary second team and asserts `team2 ? true : false`, so it silently degrades when no second team exists. Create a dedicated second team in `beforeAll` (tracking it for deletion in `afterAll`), always create the pending membership, and assert `expect(result).toBe(true)` unconditionally.

findings.title: Test users are leaked when an assertion fails
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts`, test users are deleted inline after assertions, so a failing assertion leaks user rows. Add a `createdUserIds` array alongside `createdMembershipIds`, push each created user's id, and delete them in `afterEach` after the memberships are cleared. Then remove the inline `prisma.user.delete` and manual membership cleanup calls from each test.

findings.title: Single-quoted string is inconsistent with the file's style
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx` line 35, change `session.user.email || ''` back to double quotes (`""`) to match the repo's formatting conventions.

findings.title: Good: Prisma access moved into the repository, and the server-side guard is in the right place
findings.body: Moving the inline `prisma.membership.findFirst` out of ::file{file="packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts"} into `MembershipRepository` follows the "no prisma outside repositories" rule. Checking in the getting-started server component, after the session check and before rendering, prevents the plan-selection flash that a client-side redirect would cause. Once the two logic bugs are fixed, this is a clean approach. Selecting only `id` keeps the query minimal.
